guides.title: Share volume and dollar notional trade volume are different measurements
guides.concept: Share volume counts shares; dollar notional multiplies each executed quantity by its own matched trade price.
guides.procedure: Step 1 — Establish the fictional data's as-of time and units. Step 2 — Multiply each executed share quantity by its actual fictional print price, then sum those notionals; report share total separately. Step 3 — Recheck the denominator, use only available information and distinguish a calculation from an actual market result.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: 600 shares printed at $12.00 and 400 at $12.50 imply 1,000 traded shares but $7,200+$5,000=$12,200 of total print notional.
guides.limit: A single OHLC candle and its share volume alone do not reconstruct exact transaction-level notional when individual prices are missing.
guides.invalidation: This teaching conclusion must be withheld if an observed input is absent, the timestamps are incompatible, the denominator is invalid, or the declared assumptions fail. guides.title: A quoted spread percentage depends on the reference price used in its denominator
guides.concept: The quoted bid-ask spread in dollars can be divided by the simultaneous midpoint to express a relative spread for teaching.
guides.procedure: Step 1 — Establish the fictional data's as-of time and units. Step 2 — At the same valid quote timestamp, compute midpoint=(bid+ask)/2 and spread=ask−bid, then 100×spread/midpoint only when midpoint is positive. Step 3 — Recheck the denominator, use only available information and distinguish a calculation from an actual market result.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Bid $10.00 and ask $10.10 give midpoint $10.05, width $0.10 and a midpoint-relative width of about 0.995%.

guides.title: Basis points convert a defined percentage change into hundredths of one percent
guides.concept: One basis point is one hundredth of one percentage point and can express price or rate changes with declared context.
guides.procedure: Step 1 — Establish the fictional data's as-of time and units. Step 2 — Compute 100×(new−old)/old to obtain percent change, then multiply that percentage by 100 for basis points.
